critiques.concern: Finding 2's test plan is factually wrong and its security invariant is unenforced. The existing `test_tampered_local_env_refuses` parametrize (test_lifecycle_failsafe.py:240-252) asserts rc==1 for FOUR cases, but TWO of them — `/no/such/python` (:243) and `/usr/bin/python --foo` (:242) — are absolute, non-symlink, ABSENT-path values (I confirmed: is_file()==False, exists()==False, no symlink component) that the proposed carve flips to DEGRADE (rc==0). The proposal frames its test work as additive ('assert the tamper cases still raise') and mis-cites ':246-261 tampered -> refuse' as unchanged, so the suite goes RED and the author appears not to have traced it. Worse: there is NO existing test for a genuinely present-but-non-executable file — the only 'not executable' entry (:243) is actually absent — so the invariant the proposal leans on ('every other strict violation still raises', the security-load-bearing half) is currently UNTESTED and the proposal claims it is 'enforced by extending test_lifecycle_failsafe.py'.

critiques.suggested_fix: Rewrite the plan's test section: RELOCATE :242 and :243 out of the refuse parametrize into the new degrade-with-guidance test, and ADD a genuinely present-but-non-executable case (a real file, no +x bit, via _make_exe without chmod) plus a present-but-a-directory case to the refuse list, so 'tamper stays fatal' is actually exercised. critiques.concern: The appended-argument case exposes a hole in Finding 2's security story. The value `/usr/bin/python --foo` was designed to be REFUSED as an appended-argument tamper (see the code comment at lifecycle.py:370-374: 'An appended-argument string like "/usr/bin/python -c ..." is caught by the is_file() check'). Under the carve, that string resolves to a non-existent path and DEGRADES to fallback. The runtime outcome stays safe (args discarded; fallback is the stdlib interpreter), but the proposal's clean claim 'everything else stays fatal / only pure absence degrades' is imprecise: an appended-argument tamper IS 'pure absence' at the path level. The edge-case inventory never addresses a tamper-shaped-but-nonexistent value.
critiques.suggested_fix: Decide and document the intended behavior for a value that both looks like a tamper AND doesn't exist as a path. Either (a) accept degrade and state explicitly that appended-argument/typo values now degrade-not-refuse (safe because we never execute the recorded value), updating the :242 comment and the security argument; or (b) keep such shapes fatal by checking the raw string before the exists() carve.

consolidated.steelman: The proposal is structurally disciplined and its breakers are reproduced, not hypothetical. It follows the accepted review-record-integrity shape — fix-the-instance + guard-the-class — with four narrow, independently-revertable fixes, honest Alternatives, and explicit split offers to the Maintainer (Alternatives 3/4). The load-bearing mechanics reproduce exactly on inspection across all three reads: the phantom `/good-morning` command (cli.py:487, with the real invitation self-healing at lifecycle.py:614), the `skipped-vendor-absent` filter (cli.py:502-504), the F2 stale-binding hard-fail (lifecycle.py:387-390), and F3's seed-vs-roster drift. Crucially, F3 reuses `strip_conditional_regions`/`cairn:if` (config.py:1004-1024, already wired at install.py:251-252) rather than inventing a mechanism — the exact trap the superseded proposal fell into. It clears the two hard-won traps: doctrine is quoted accurately (session-routines.md:66-67 is a verbatim, in-context match) and the "no doctrine change / rate-limit N/A" call is correct — no doctrine/ file is altered and a grep of doctrine/ confirms no rule codifies the local-env.json interpreter trust root, so the gate genuinely does not apply; the proposal even pre-empts the "should it be codified?" question and hands it to review. F2's carve is narrow (absence-only), preserving the fail-closed tamper posture, and F2's "only pure absence degrades" instinct is right. The AST re-anchor obligation is acknowledged and kept Maintainer-supervised, and the session-start --dry-run feature is correctly deferred. For the adopter lens: none of the four fixes ADD apparatus a solo postdoc must staff — they are subtractive/corrective (dual-review never-over-staff and rationale Anchor 12 both satisfied). The proposal recommends External + Security-Review and proactively surfaces its own scope tensions.

numbered_critiques.concern: Finding 2's test plan is factually wrong and its security invariant is unenforced. The existing test_tampered_local_env_refuses parametrize (test_lifecycle_failsafe.py:240-252) asserts rc==1 for FOUR cases, but TWO — /no/such/python (:243) and /usr/bin/python --foo (:242) — are absolute, non-symlink, ABSENT-path values (is_file()==False, exists()==False, no symlink component) that the proposed carve flips to DEGRADE (rc==0). The proposal frames its test work as additive ('assert the tamper cases still raise') and mis-cites ':246-261 tampered -> refuse' as unchanged, so the suite goes RED and the author appears not to have traced it. Worse: there is NO existing test for a genuinely present-but-non-executable file — the only 'not executable' entry (:243) is actually absent — so the invariant the proposal leans on ('every other strict violation still raises', the security-load-bearing half) is currently UNTESTED even though the proposal claims it is 'enforced by extending test_lifecycle_failsafe.py'.
numbered_critiques.grounding: bootstrap/tests/test_lifecycle_failsafe.py:240-252 (read this session) + python repro this session: both :242 and :243 are absolute/non-symlink/absent -> would_degrade under the carve.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Rewrite the plan's test section: RELOCATE :242 and :243 out of the refuse parametrize into the new degrade-with-guidance test, and ADD a genuinely present-but-non-executable case (a real file, no +x bit, via _make_exe without chmod) plus a present-but-a-directory case to the refuse list, so 'tamper stays fatal' is actually exercised. Correct the ':246-261 unchanged' citation.

numbered_critiques.concern: Finding 2's 'synthesis of two existing doctrines, not a new rule' framing overstates its doctrinal cover: both cited passages carry the matching words but govern DIFFERENT subjects. runtime-contract.md:139/162/171 is the 'degraded-assurance / named-forfeiture' state for an adopter running below the full QA aid set (absent degradable aids like claim_check/link_check — table at :143-149), and session-routines.md:416 is an informational drift check (doctrine-conformance reads it as the upgrade --plan adoption-drift check at :407-419; scope-adopter reads it as the fold-back drift status line at :414-418 — 'never blocks work'). F2 is a genuinely NEW (narrow, defensible) behavior at a security surface; presenting analogy as citation is the same failure class as a misquote (right words, wrong load-bearing referent) and an External/Security reviewer will test it. (The 'no doctrine change -> rate-limit N/A' claim itself still holds — grep confirms no doctrine/ file codifies the interpreter fail-closed posture — so this is a framing correction, not a rate-limit violation.)

numbered_critiques.concern: SCOPE — the bundle mixes risk classes such that F2's Security-Review GATES the Decision on the unambiguous fixes. Per the proposal's own plan-review line, External + Security-Review are recommended before the Decision for ALL FOUR findings. So F1 (delete a phantom command — a zero-risk, unambiguous pure win) and F4 (align text to doctrine) cannot land until a security review of the F2 trust-root carve completes. For a one-shot, imminent install that is real cost — the 'different risk classes -> different proposals' pattern that forced a prior split. Four proposals would be disproportionate ceremony against the deadline (Cairn warns against over-apparatus) and the coherent-theme bundling is otherwise good; the fix is to decouple the Decision.

numbered_critiques.concern: The appended-argument case exposes a hole in Finding 2's security story. The value /usr/bin/python --foo was designed to be REFUSED as an appended-argument tamper (code comment at lifecycle.py:370-374: 'An appended-argument string like ... is caught by the is_file() check'). Under the carve, that string resolves to a non-existent path and DEGRADES to fallback. The runtime outcome stays safe (args discarded; fallback is the stdlib interpreter), but the proposal's clean claim 'everything else stays fatal / only pure absence degrades' is imprecise: an appended-argument tamper IS 'pure absence' at the path level. The edge-case inventory never addresses a tamper-shaped-but-nonexistent value.
numbered_critiques.suggested_fix: Decide and document the intended behavior for a value that both looks like a tamper AND doesn't exist as a path. Either (a) accept degrade and state explicitly that appended-argument/typo values now degrade-not-refuse (safe because we never execute the recorded value), updating the :242 comment and the security argument; or (b) keep such shapes fatal by checking the raw string before the exists() carve.

consolidated.second_round_recommendation: Yes — unanimous across all three lenses, and the proposal itself requests it. Recommend an External cross-type pass plus a Security-Review before the Decision. Finding 2 edits a security trust root whose function already carries prior review-finding annotations (lifecycle.py:361-362,370-375 cite 'finding 1/4'), so a fresh security read of the absent-vs-tamper branch boundary is warranted — and R1 shows the claimed enforcement of 'tamper stays fatal' does not exist as a test while R5 shows an appended-argument tamper shape now degrades rather than refuses; those are exactly the judgments a Security-Review + cross-type External read should adjudicate, not an Internal same-type read. The engine edit in Finding 3 (install.py, a high-risk surface) also trips the AST-attestation baseline and warrants the External track. Sequence per R4: let F1/F4 (and, once R2 is corrected, F3's template markers) be acceptable on the Internal read so the pure-win phantom-command fix is not held hostage, and route only the F2 trust-root carve and the engine AST re-anchor through the External/Security track. Critically, the second round should proceed AFTER the author (a) rewrites the Finding-2 test design and decides/documents the appended-argument behavior (R1, R5) and (b) corrects the Finding-3 high-rigor-legacy factual error and non-reproducing 4/2/0 count (R2), so the External panel reviews accurate evidence rather than re-finding these.
